item.content:encoded: Republic of Ireland defender Jimmy Dunne has been named as one of two reserve goalkeepers for his side's Nations League clash with Israel. Dunne's positional switch comes about after [USN:L1N45I02P TEXT:"Gavin Bazunu withdrew"] from the squad for the game over Israel's war in Gaza. The Irish team engaged in [USN:L6N45I06Z TEXT:"hours of discussions"] over whether to boycott the game against Israel, with a majority eventually voting to play. UEFA rules require teams to register three goalkeepers for Nations League games. The game takes place in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday evening.

item.title: Men arrested in major incident at UK air base used by US
item.description: British police arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences near an airbase used by the US to strike Iranian targets, while Army bomb disposal experts searched vehicles and homes were evacuated in the "major incident" on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Toby Shepheard
item.content:encoded: British police arrested several men on suspicion of explosives offences near an airbase used by the US to strike Iranian targets, while Army bomb disposal experts searched vehicles and homes were evacuated in the "major incident" on Sunday. The British government, which gave authorisation to the US to use [USN:L1N4080WS TEXT:"RAF Fairford"] to strike Iranian missile sites that were attacking ships in the Strait of Hormuz, said Prime Minister Andy Burnham was being updated about the incident. Iran's Revolutionary Guards had warned in July that any base used in strikes would be a legitimate target. A Reuters eyewitness said armed police had blocked access to the main gate of the base, while machinery had been positioned in front of access points. Residents of a nearby village were woken in the early hours and ordered to leave their homes. Around 30 emergency vehicles, including police cars, ambulances and fire engines, were parked up in the village of Fairford near the base, while a helicopter flew above. DECLARATION OF A MAJOR INCIDENT "A number of properties are currently being evacuated in the Whelford area following the declaration of a major incident. It follows the arrest of several men on suspicion of offences under the Explosives Act," Gloucestershire police said in a statement, referring to a village near the air base. "The Army's specialist explosive ordnance disposal team are currently examining a number of vehicles." Police said they believed the incident was now contained. The Daily Mail website carried a photograph of five topless men being arrested while another photograph showed three large white vans parked nearby. Live footage of the scene from broadcasters showed a bomb disposal robot operating near to the three vans. Local media said counter-terrorism police were leading the investigation. The British government said it would be inappropriate to comment whilst investigations are ongoing. A spokesperson for the US Air Force declined to discuss specific force protection measures. "The 501st Combat Support Wing and our fellow UK-based Wings remain vigilant and will take appropriate actions to ensure the safety and security of our US service members, civilians, contractors, and their families," the spokesperson said. "We constantly assess a variety of factors that determine what measures we institute or modify to protect our installations, our people and their families." Britain said in July its armed forces were [USN:L1N43P14J TEXT:"ready to protect"] the country from any attack after Iran's Revolutionary Guards warned the UK not to allow US bombers to fly from Fairford. Media reports said security had been increased at other bases used by the US in Britain, including at Lakenheath and Mildenhall. British ministers have also previously briefed providers of critical infrastructure on the [USN:L8N45H0EB TEXT:"threat posed by Russia"], with the government increasingly concerned about possible sabotage operations and cyberattacks. Russia denies mounting hybrid attacks on Western nations.

item.title: Former Angel Taylor Ward delivers game-winner for Mariners
item.description: Pinch hitter Taylor Ward hit a tiebreaking two-run single against his former team in the seventh inning and J.P. Crawford homered on the next pitch as the Seattle Mariners defeated the visiting Los Angeles Angels 8-4 Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Taylor Ward hit a tiebreaking two-run single against his former team in the seventh inning and J.P. Crawford homered on the next pitch as the Seattle Mariners defeated the visiting Los Angeles Angels 8-4 Saturday night. Rookie Michael Arroyo had three hits and Cole Young scored three times for the Mariners (75-86), who snapped a two-game losing streak. Seattle got a scare when left-hander Kade Anderson, their prized pitching prospect, was hit near his pitching elbow by a 103.8 mph liner from Angels second baseman Christian Moore in the fourth. Anderson, who pitched 3 1/3 scoreless innings, was immediately taken out, and the Mariners later announced he sustained a bruised left forearm. Mariners reliever Carlos Vargas (3-0) got the victory and Angels left-hander Mitch Farris (1-4) took the loss. Bryce Teodosio had a two-run single in a four-run sixth to help the Angels (62-99) overcome a 4-0 deficit. Los Angeles will need to win its season finale to avoid the first 100-loss campaign in franchise history. The Angels are the only major league team that has not lost 100 games in a season. The Mariners opened the scoring in the second. Young drew a one-out walk and advanced to second on Arroyo's line-drive single to center. Rookie Lazaro Montes then hit a ground-rule double into the right field corner to plate Young. Seattle doubled its advantage in the fourth. Young drew a leadoff walk before Arroyo lined a single to left. Young tagged and took third on Montes' flyout to right before Leo Rivas lifted a sacrifice fly to center. The Mariners scored again in the fifth as Randy Arozarena led off with an infield single and took third on Dominic Canzone's double to right. One out later, Josh Naylor hit a chopper to first baseman Vaughn Grissom, with Arozarena just beating the throw home with a head-first slide. Young then grounded an RBI single to center to make it 4-0. The Angels tied it with four runs in the sixth. Teodosio lined a two-run single to center before Wade Meckler scored on Tyler Heineman's squeeze bunt to pull Los Angeles within 4-3. After a one-out walk to Mike Trout, the Mariners brought in Vargas. Jose Siri grounded out to third, allowing Teodosio to score the tying run. Angels starter Ryan Johnson allowed four runs on seven hits over five innings. The right-hander walked four and struck out three. --Field Level Media

item.title: Fury-Joshua fight in doubt as White uncertain over blockbuster bout
item.description: Plans for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's long-awaited heavyweight clash were in doubt on Saturday after promoter Dana White said he was unsure whether the fight would go ahead.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Plans for Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua's long-awaited heavyweight clash were in doubt on Saturday after promoter Dana White said he was unsure whether the fight would go ahead. Fury and Joshua were announced on Thursday as opponents for a December 11 showdown at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, a contest billed as one of the biggest fights in British boxing history. However, Fury said in a video posted on social media late on Friday that the [USN:L6N45I030 TEXT:"fight was in jeopardy"] because Joshua and his promoter, Eddie Hearn, were trying to withdraw from the all-British heavyweight showdown between the former world champions. Hearn's promotional company, Matchroom Boxing, did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent on Saturday. White, the UFC president and head of Zuffa Boxing, told reporters in London on Saturday that he did not know whether the bout would proceed as planned. Asked about a scheduled press conference in coming days, White said he was also uncertain whether it would take place. Hearn has said he and Joshua had insisted on the bout being staged in Britain, while the promoters had proposed holding it in New York's Madison Square Garden. The dispute over promotional rights has also sparked claims of contractual breaches and talk of replacement opponents.

item.title: East German espionage raised GDP by 7.4% in late 1980s, study finds
item.description: East Germany's extensive Cold War economic espionage in the 1970s and 1980s lifted its overall economic output by 7.4% at the end of the 1980s, according to a study by the Rockwool Foundation Berlin, seen by Reuters on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Maria Martinez, Rene Wagner
item.content:encoded: East Germany's extensive Cold War economic espionage in the 1970s and 1980s lifted its overall economic output by 7.4% at the end of the 1980s, according to a study by the Rockwool Foundation Berlin, seen by Reuters on Sunday. Here are some more details: Industrial value added was 22.3% higher due to espionage, equivalent to 20.2 billion East German marks, or €4.1 billion ($4.7 billion) in 2020 prices. All estimates refer to 1988, the year before the Berlin Wall fell. Co-author Adrian Lerche said the findings had present-day relevance as governments tighten export controls, screen foreign investment and seek to protect strategic technologies. The Stasi, East Germany's sprawling intelligence service, helped companies obtain scientific and technical information from Western businesses and research institutions. Firms receiving useful intelligence recorded faster productivity growth, invested more and concentrated more on core products. "Stasi espionage strengthened East Germany's position within the socialist bloc," said Albrecht Glitz, co-author of the study. "It did not, however, significantly improve success in Western markets." The gains also spread through supplier and customer networks, supporting broader economic effects, the researchers said. Each additional valuable piece of information produced an estimated annual return of about €330,000 in 2020 prices. ($1 = 0.8770 euros)

item.title: France La moitié des sièges du Sénat renouvelée, le RN espère un groupe
item.description: La moitié du Sénat français est renouvelée ce dimanche lors d'élections au suffrage universel indirect dont l'un des principaux enjeux est la capacité du Rassemblement national (RN) à constituer un groupe, soit au moins dix élus.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La moitié du Sénat français est renouvelée ce dimanche lors d'élections au suffrage universel indirect dont l'un des principaux enjeux est la capacité du Rassemblement national (RN) à constituer un groupe, soit au moins dix élus. Un total de 178 sièges - sur 348 - est remis en jeu cette année à la chambre haute, renouvelée à 50% tous les trois ans via un collège de "grands électeurs", maires et délégués de conseils municipaux pour la plupart. Premier parti d'opposition à l'Assemblée nationale, le RN de Marine Le Pen, candidate à l'élection présidentielle de 2027, compte jusqu'ici trois sénateurs. Sa percée lors des élections municipales de mars, en particulier dans les communes du pourtour méditerranéen, lui permet d'espérer améliorer sa représentativité au Sénat où la droite républicaine est majoritaire depuis les années 1970 - à l'exception d'une parenthèse socialiste entre 2011 et 2014. A gauche, les écologistes pourraient reculer après la perte de plusieurs mairies au printemps et La France insoumise espère faire son entrée au palais du Luxembourg en décrochant au moins un siège. Avant le scrutin de ce dimanche, le groupe Les Républicains du Sénat comptait 131 sièges, devant le groupe Socialiste, écologiste et républicain (64 sièges).

item.title: Swiss voters set to reject tighter neutrality rules that would curb NATO cooperation
item.description: The proposal, supported by the right-wing Swiss People's Party, called for a more restrictive form of neutrality that would have blocked their country from imposing economic sanctions or cooperating with NATO.
item.dc:creator: Marleen Kaesebier, John Revill
item.content:encoded: Swiss voters on Sunday looked set to reject a proposal to adopt a more restrictive form of neutrality that would have blocked their country from imposing economic sanctions or cooperating with NATO. More than two-thirds voted against a proposal for a strictly defined version of neutrality to be written into the Swiss constitution, according to the latest referendum projections by state broadcaster SRF. While Swiss neutrality has been internationally recognised since the end of the Napoleonic wars in 1815, how the government implements it is not spelled out. The right-wing Swiss People's Party (SVP) has said that Switzerland's traditional position has been eroded after Bern imposed sanctions on Russia following its invasion of Ukraine . The campaign has funded posters across the country urging people to vote "No war, yes to neutrality", featuring white peace doves, ahead of the vote. SWISS GOVERNMENT, MOST PARTIES OPPOSE THE PROPOSAL Apart from the SVP, most parties and the Swiss government oppose the proposal, with Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis saying it would harm national security and prevent Switzerland from training with NATO. The Green Party and the smaller Evangelical People's Party (EVP) expressed relief over Sunday's projections. "Voters understood what the SVP wanted: it wanted Switzerland to isolate itself internationally and shirk its responsibilities when international law is being trampled on," said Sibel Arslan, a lawmaker for the Green Party. The SVP meanwhile accepted the defeat and said it currently had no plans for further action. "I'm of course not pleased with the result," said SVP lawmaker Lukas Reimann, adding that the commitment to Swiss neutrality expressed by all sides during the campaign was encouraging. "It is absolutely clear that neutrality belongs to Switzerland and is part of Switzerland's identity," he said. "Going forward, we will judge the opponents of the initiative by that commitment." If the government or opponents of the initiative were to stray from neutrality, for example by adopting tougher sanctions, the party would need to become active again, Reimann said. 'SWISS VOTERS LIKE NEUTRALITY' Fabio Wasserfallen, a professor of European politics at the University of Bern, said before the vote: "Swiss voters like neutrality, but they approve of how the government is implementing it at present." "They are also generally in favour of the sanctions on Russia over the war in Ukraine, and don't want that to change." The [USN:L8N44F0X5 TEXT:"campaign"] wanted the constitution to stipulate that Switzerland cannot join or cooperate with any military or defence alliance unless attacked, and that it refrain from joining any sanctions unless approved by the United Nations. It says Swiss neutrality has served the country well in the past, keeping it out of both world wars, and also helps Bern offer its 'good offices' to help negotiate peace between warring parties. "Switzerland has not had a war for 200 years because it is permanently armed and neutral," Christoph Blocher, the billionaire businessman and backer of the SVP, said ahead of the vote. "But neutrality has been followed less and less in recent years," he told Reuters, with Russia now seeing Switzerland as a party to the conflict because of the sanctions.

item.title: South African police probe mining feud, business rivalry after shootings kill 27
item.description: South African police were on Sunday hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country's problem with gun violence.
item.dc:creator: Xolani Nhlapo, Esa Alexander
item.content:encoded: South African police were on Sunday hunting the perpetrators of two separate shootings that killed 27 people within hours of each other, in stark reminders of the country's problem with gun violence. Officials were still establishing the motives for the shootings near Johannesburg and Cape Town, but initial investigations suggested one could be a turf war between illegal miners and the other a business rivalry. Violent crime remains rife in South Africa, despite government efforts to curb one of the highest per-capita murder rates in the world. In Wedela township, about 80 km (50 miles) from Johannesburg, 17 people were killed and 15 injured at a tavern when suspects armed with AK-47 rifles opened fire at around 9:30 p.m. (1930 GMT) on Saturday, according to police. SHOOTING COULD BE RETALIATION Many residents were reluctant to speak about the incident, but one said that illegal miners, known locally as zama zamas from an isiZulu expression for "taking a chance", live in the area, where powerful gangs control the illicit gold mining trade. The province's police commissioner Tommy Mthombeni told reporters on the scene that one line of inquiry was that the shooting was a "turf war in terms of illegal mining". There was a shooting at the same tavern about a month ago and Saturday's shooting could be retaliation for that, he added. NO ARRESTS YET Soldiers from the national army and police pathologists had arrived in the township, where two burnt vehicles could be seen. The tavern where the shooting happened had a sign that read "No weapons allowed" below its trading hours. At the scene of the shooting in Lwandle, on the outskirts of Cape Town, onlookers had gathered behind police lines but did not want to speak to journalists, saying they feared for their safety. In that incident, gunmen opened fire in a venue selling grilled meat around 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, killing 10 people and injuring 11 more. An eyewitness video from the venue shows people dancing and singing in a crowded outdoor area when a burst of shots rings out and screams are heard. A police official there said "a business jealousy might have been the issue," as there were reports that people had been buying alcohol in cheaper places and going to the venue to drink. No arrests have been made yet and detectives are working to find the gunmen, police said in statements. "South Africa has a serious illegal firearms problem, and firearms are frequently used by organised criminal groups as well as in gang-related and other violent crimes," said crime expert Yusuf Abramjee. THREAT TO DEMOCRACY "Every mass shooting should therefore trigger more than an investigation into the immediate perpetrators," he told Reuters. "Authorities need to look at the wider networks behind the violence." Crime is expected to be a major issue for voters in municipal elections in November, when the African National Congress is facing further erosion of voter support. President Cyril Ramaphosa said earlier this year that organised crime had become the biggest threat to South Africa's democracy, and [USN:L1N4010N8 TEXT:"deployed the army"] to help police in some areas. A shooting at a house party near Durban on Tuesday night [USN:L1N45F058 TEXT:"killed 11 people"], while a [USN:L8N45912N TEXT:"series of women's bodies"] found near Johannesburg since July has renewed fear and anger over high rates of femicide.

item.title: India badminton medallist says Aichi-Nagoya Asiad 'sad' for athletes
item.description: India badminton medallist H.S. Prannoy has criticised Asian Games organisers for putting on a "sad" event for athletes and arranging a "cruel" competition schedule for his sport.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India badminton medallist H.S. Prannoy has criticised Asian Games organisers for putting on a "sad" event for athletes and arranging a "cruel" competition schedule for his sport. Prannoy, who won a men's team bronze at the Aichi-Nagoya Games, said the lack of a dedicated athletes' village had taken away the joy of mixing with other competitors, who had been spread across hotels, temporary wooden units and a cruise ship. "The whole fun and the whole point of multi-sport events is you get to meet the rest of the players," he said in a video interview posted on the Badminton Association of India's YouTube channel on Saturday. "There is an opportunity to mingle with them. There is an opportunity to have a conversation with them. We only felt that when we went for the opening ceremony. “It was literally sad to be in such a situation." Prannoy said the Games compared poorly to his experience at the last Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, where he was part of the silver medal-winning men's team. "Straight from China, you expect things to be better three-four years later but in this event, (it went) downwards. A lot of (athletes) had difficult experiences in terms of accommodation and transport. “It was just a mediocre event, to be honest." Aichi-Nagoya organisers did not immediately respond on Sunday to a request for comment on Prannoy's remarks. On Saturday, an Aichi-Nagoya Games organising committee official [USN:L6N45I02K TEXT:"apologised"] for logistical mistakes that have affected athletes, saying accommodation and transport had improved and that staff were working "to identify the causes of each mistake and make sure they don't happen again". A number of athletes and teams have complained of logistical problems at the Games, ranging from long waits to check in to their rooms, to transport glitches. Prannoy also criticised the badminton scheduling, noting players in the singles tournament had competed in two matches a day, one more than usual. "It's cruel because everybody is aiming for a good Asian Games, which comes once in four years. To have two singles games in a day, I haven't seen it like that in ages," said Prannoy.

item.title: US consulate builder in Milan to pay $35 million over labour probe
item.description: US builder Caddell Construction has formally committed to pay €30.941 million ($35.24 million) in a probe into alleged worker exploitation at the site of the new US consulate in Milan, a document seen by Reuters showed.
item.dc:creator: Emilio Parodi
item.content:encoded: US builder Caddell Construction has formally committed to pay €30.941 million ($35.24 million) in a probe into alleged worker exploitation at the site of the new US consulate in Milan, a document seen by Reuters showed. The Alabama-based construction giant undertook to pay nearly €20 million to workers in overtime, accommodation reimbursements and compensation for non-material damages, according to a document submitted by the firm to Milan prosecutors. It did not admit any liability. Caddell did not respond to a request for comment. In a statement issued in June, Caddell said it was proactively cooperating with judicial authorities and was "committed to treating and paying workers fairly". Italy's labour minister described the operation as "one of the most significant crackdowns on labour exploitation in recent years". "This outcome strengthens Italy's reputation internationally and sends a clear message... that the state does not abandon its most vulnerable workers", Labour Minister Marina Calderone said in a statement on Sunday. The company specialises in large-scale projects, including contracts for US embassies and military facilities. Caddell Construction's Italian unit was placed under [USN:L8N4252B5 TEXT:"investigation"] for alleged labour exploitation and put under judicial administration on May 29, a measure [USN:L8N42H0TF TEXT:"upheld by a judge"] two weeks later. Milan prosecutors and Italy's Carabinieri police accused the company of recruiting workers in India through an intermediary based in New Delhi and employing them on "exhausting shifts, underpaid, without safety protections and under the constant threat of dismissal". The company has also agreed to pay more than €7 million to Italy's social security agency INPS and almost €4 million to the Labour Inspectorate, the document showed. In the letter to Milan prosecutors, signed by Caddell Construction executive officer Michael Angelo Ranieri and reviewed by Reuters, the US company stressed that its commitments did not amount to any admission of wrongdoing. "Furthermore, they do not imply any acceptance of the legal and factual assessments made by the authorities involved," it added. CASE AGAINST COMPANY SET TO BE DISMISSED AFTER PAYMENT Two sources with direct knowledge of the matter said the agreement involves the regularisation of around 500 workers, the recognition by the Italian state of residence permits for 270 foreign workers and unemployment benefits for 60 workers who had been dismissed. One of the two sources said that, once the payments had been made, Milan prosecutors were expected to seek the dismissal of the case against Caddell's Italian unit. The source added that prosecutors were expected to pursue plea bargain agreements with two Caddell executives arrested as part of the investigation. Construction on the US consulate in Milan started in 2022. The contract was worth almost $210 million and work was initially scheduled to finish in 2025, but this date was subsequently put back to 2028. A US State Department spokesperson told Reuters in June that US law enforcement was cooperating with the Italian authorities, and that "the US government does not tolerate labour exploitation". This is the latest in a series of labour exploitation investigations conducted in recent years by [USN:L8N42U15N TEXT:"Milan prosecutor"] Paolo Storari. The probes have forced companies to grant fuller employment rights to more than 60,000 workers and enabled authorities to recover more than €1 billion ($1.1 billion), while also fuelling a heated debate over whether Italy's judiciary is overstepping its role. ($1 = 0.8779 euros)

item.title: Former Angel Taylor Ward delivers game-winner for Mariners
item.description: Pinch hitter Taylor Ward hit a tiebreaking two-run single against his former team in the seventh inning and J.P. Crawford homered on the next pitch as the Seattle Mariners defeated the visiting Los Angeles Angels 8-4 Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Taylor Ward hit a tiebreaking two-run single against his former team in the seventh inning and J.P. Crawford homered on the next pitch as the Seattle Mariners defeated the visiting Los Angeles Angels 8-4 Saturday night. Rookie Michael Arroyo had three hits and Cole Young scored three times for the Mariners (75-86), who snapped a two-game losing streak. Seattle got a scare when left-hander Kade Anderson, their prized pitching prospect, was hit near his pitching elbow by a 103.8 mph liner from Angels second baseman Christian Moore in the fourth. Anderson, who pitched 3 1/3 scoreless innings, was immediately taken out, and the Mariners later announced he sustained a bruised left forearm. Mariners reliever Carlos Vargas (3-0) got the victory and Angels left-hander Mitch Farris (1-4) took the loss. Bryce Teodosio had a two-run single in a four-run sixth to help the Angels (62-99) overcome a 4-0 deficit. Los Angeles will need to win its season finale to avoid the first 100-loss campaign in franchise history. The Angels are the only major league team that has not lost 100 games in a season. The Mariners opened the scoring in the second. Young drew a one-out walk and advanced to second on Arroyo's line-drive single to center. Rookie Lazaro Montes then hit a ground-rule double into the right field corner to plate Young. Seattle doubled its advantage in the fourth. Young drew a leadoff walk before Arroyo lined a single to left. Young tagged and took third on Montes' flyout to right before Leo Rivas lifted a sacrifice fly to center. The Mariners scored again in the fifth as Randy Arozarena led off with an infield single and took third on Dominic Canzone's double to right. One out later, Josh Naylor hit a chopper to first baseman Vaughn Grissom, with Arozarena just beating the throw home with a head-first slide. Young then grounded an RBI single to center to make it 4-0. The Angels tied it with four runs in the sixth. Teodosio lined a two-run single to center before Wade Meckler scored on Tyler Heineman's squeeze bunt to pull Los Angeles within 4-3. After a one-out walk to Mike Trout, the Mariners brought in Vargas. Jose Siri grounded out to third, allowing Teodosio to score the tying run. Angels starter Ryan Johnson allowed four runs on seven hits over five innings. The right-hander walked four and struck out three. --Field Level Media

item.title: OpenAI, Anthropic CEOs called to appear at Australian AI probe
item.description: A rogue OpenAI bot hacked the country's health-system database earlier this month.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic have been called to appear at an Australian Senate inquiry on AI, the head of the probe said on Sunday, days after the revelation that a [USN:L4N45F1EW TEXT:"rogue OpenAI bot"] had hacked the country's health-system database. The Medicare breach, condemned by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, is one of the highest-profile incidents of AI agents accessing external systems outside the US. OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei have been sent written requests to appear at the inquiry, which is to hold public hearings in the capital Canberra on Thursday, said a spokesperson for Senator Sarah Hanson-Young of the Australian Greens party, who chairs the probe. OpenAI and Anthropic did not immediately respond to requests for comment outside business hours. The OpenAI agent's incursion on one of the country's most used government agencies may prompt Albanese's Labor government to [USN:L4N45G0G8 TEXT:"toughen AI-specific laws"] it is readying for next year, adding pressure to Australia-US relations already tested by Canberra's ban on social media for teens, tech policy experts say. The Senate inquiry is examining the potential impacts of AI and data centres on Australian communities, industries, water and energy. It is one of several state and federal probes into AI. "There are serious questions for Sam Altman to answer about the OpenAI hack of Australian government websites," Hanson-Young said in a statement. Altman and Amodei "must front up, face the Senate's questions and have an honest conversation about what effective, lasting regulation of this industry should look like", she said. Albanese, who revealed the June breach of Medicare on Thursday, called it "unacceptable", saying he had voiced "extreme concern" to Altman. OpenAI says it only learned of the breach — one of at least four of Australian government websites — in August. It says the incident was not intentional and did not compromise any private information.

item.title: Une marche orangiste autorisée en Irlande du Nord
item.description: La Haute Cour d'Irlande du Nord a autorisé tôt dimanche une marche protestant à traverser un quartier catholique, annulant ainsi une interdiction provisoire décidée la veille.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Ferguson
item.content:encoded: La Haute Cour d'Irlande du Nord a autorisé tôt dimanche une marche protestant à traverser un quartier catholique, annulant ainsi une interdiction provisoire décidée la veille. Le tribunal a rejeté une nouvelle requête visant à empêcher l'Ordre Orange de traverser un quartier catholique de Portadown, après que la Cour d'appel eut annulé une injonction provisoire accordée samedi aux habitants qui s'opposaient au défilé. Les habitants du quartier de Garvaghy Road avaient contesté la décision rendue vendredi par la Commission des défilés d'Irlande du Nord, qui autorisait les Orangistes à défiler dans leur rue, une enclave catholique au sein d'une ville majoritairement protestante, mettant ainsi fin à une interdiction de près de 30 ans. La Première ministre d'Irlande du Nord, Michelle O'Neill, et la présidente du parti nationaliste irlandais Sinn Féin, Mary Lou McDonald, se trouvaient dans la foule s'est rassemblée tôt dimanche matin à Garvaghy Road pour protester contre la décision de la Cour. "Même si les forces du mal veulent nous empêcher de créer une nouvelle Irlande unifiée, elles échoueront", a dit Mary Lou McDonald à la foule. Carla Lockhart, députée du Parti unioniste démocratique, a déclaré aux journalistes devant le tribunal qu'il appartenait au Sinn Féin et aux autres responsables politiques nationalistes de respecter l'Etat de droit et de permettre au défilé de passer. Ce trajet avait été interdit en 1998, année où l'accord de paix du Vendredi Saint, qui a mis fin à trois décennies de violences politiques et communautaires en Irlande du Nord, a été conclu. La décision rendue vendredi par la Commission des défilés stipulait que seulement 35 personnes, un nombre inférieur à la normale, pourrait prendre part au défilé, et que celui-ci devait débuter à 08h00 (07h00 GMT) et s'achever à 09h30.

item.title: Padres clinch home field for wild-card round; D-backs remain alive
item.description: Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts homered and the San Diego Padres clinched home-field advantage in the first round of the National League playoffs with a 10-7 victory over the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Manny Machado and Xander Bogaerts homered and the San Diego Padres clinched home-field advantage in the first round of the National League playoffs with a 10-7 victory over the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks on Saturday. Machado's 30th homer of the season, a three-run opposite field shot off Jose Cabrera (0-4) in the fourth, gave the Padres (90-71) a 6-4 lead they never lost. The Padres, the No. 4 seed, will open a best-of-three NL wild-card series against the fifth-seeded Chicago Cubs on Tuesday. The D-backs (86-75) remained in the race for the final NL wild-card spot after Philadelphia (87-74) lost to Tampa Bay on Saturday. The D-backs own the tiebreaker over the Phillies and will advance if they win Sunday and the Phillies lose at home to the Rays. Arizona scored three runs off Mason Miller in the ninth but he struck out Ildemaro Vargas to end the game. Jake Cronenworth had two hits and two RBIs for the Padres, who have won eight of 10 and 16 of 19. James McCann hit a two-run homer, Tim Tawa had three hits and Ketel Marte added two hits for the D-backs, who had a season-high six-game winning streak broken. Arizona's Gabriel Moreno was 1-for-3 with an RBI single and leads the NL with a .311 batting average entering the final day of the season. Philadelphia's Luis Arraez, who is out with a sprained ankle, is hitting .310. Dustin Harris and Jackson Merrill had two hits and scored twice apiece, and Ethan Salas also collected two hits for the Padres. San Diego starter Walker Buehler gave up five hits and four runs (three earned) in 3 2/3 innings. He struck out three and walked one. Yuki Matsui (5-1) retired the only batter he faced for the win. The lead changed four times in the first four innings, with San Diego scoring twice in the third for a 3-2 lead when right fielder Corbin Carroll and center fielder Tawa could not find routine fly balls. McCann's two-run homer off Buehler made it 4-3 Arizona in the top of the fourth before Machado's blast gave the Padres the lead in the bottom of the inning. Bogaerts hit a solo shot in a two-run fifth for an 8-4 San Diego lead and Cronenworth added a two-run single in the sixth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rays collect 17 hits, blast skidding Phillies in runaway
item.description: Richie Palacios drove in four runs and Victor Mesa Jr. had four hits and two RBIs as the visiting Tampa Bay Rays walloped the Philadelphia Phillies 12-1 on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Richie Palacios drove in four runs and Victor Mesa Jr. had four hits and two RBIs as the visiting Tampa Bay Rays walloped the Philadelphia Phillies 12-1 on Saturday. Griffin Jax and six relievers took care of matters on the mound for Tampa Bay (98-63), which has already clinched the top spot in the American League playoffs. Other standouts for the Rays included Junior Caminero, who slugged his 42nd homer, and Yandy Diaz, who collected three hits and scored three runs. Tampa Bay had more hits, 17-7. In the midst of a late-season freefall, Philadelphia gave the starting nod to Aaron Nola (7-12), who threw 88 pitches on Wednesday before promptly allowing three first-inning runs. Things only got worse from there for the Phillies, who have been outscored 23-3 during a four-game slide. Philadelphia (87-74), which entered the night with a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, once again failed to cut into that number itself. However, Arizona's 10-7 loss at San Diego later Saturday reduced the magic number to one, meaning the Phillies can clinch their postseason spot with a win or a Diamondbacks loss on Sunday. Arizona owns the tiebreaker over Philadelphia. Diaz doubled to open the game and scored on Caminero's two-out home run. The Rays tacked on another run when Mesa and Palacios delivered back-to-back doubles to make it 3-0. After retiring all six hitters he faced in the first two innings, Jax worked around some issues in the third. He gave up a leadoff single before inducing a double play by J.T. Realmuto. Jax then allowed another hit before Trea Turner lined one off the pitcher's back, although it ricocheted right to shortstop Taylor Walls, who threw to first for the final out. Jax walked off gingerly and left the game, but the Tampa Bay hitters continued to pile on. The Rays scored four times in the fifth, capped by Cedric Mullins' two-run single. The sixth inning featured another scoring display by the Tampa Bay offense, as Mesa delivered an RBI double and Palacios followed with a two-run single to push the lead to 10-0. Meanwhile, Steven Matz (6-6) logged a perfect fourth inning for the Rays before Brody Hopkins had no issues in the fifth and Cam Booser worked a scoreless sixth. Manuel Rodriguez allowed an unearned run in the seventh before Ty Johnson and Cole Sulser each pitched a scoreless inning to close it out. Nola allowed three runs on four hits in one inning of work. --Field Level Media

item.title: Revitalised Russell says he can fight for victory week-in, week-out
item.description: Mercedes racer George Russell is confident he can fight for the win in every race going forward after a resounding return to form with victory in Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Takle
item.content:encoded: Mercedes racer George Russell is confident he can fight for the win in every race going forward after a resounding return to form with [USN:L1N45I03R TEXT:"victory"] in Saturday's Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The Briton capped what he called the most "dominant weekend I've had in my career", having achieved a 'grand slam' in Baku, starting from pole, leading every lap, setting the fastest lap and finishing off with a win. "I think I never lost that faith in myself," said Russell, who kept a charging Max Verstappen at bay for much of the race's closing stages. His form around a layout that rewards confidence but is known for catching drivers out stands in stark contrast to struggles earlier in a season that saw him eclipsed by 20-year-old championship-leading teammate Kimi Antonelli. The Italian has scored eight wins to Russell’s three, but Russell said work he put in to adapt his driving style to the 2026 cars over the sport's summer break had been key to his return to form. "Even through the tough moments I knew there was a reason why I was off the pace," he said. "You know, it's been four races since the break. I’ve been on the front row in three of them, three podiums from the four races. I feel I can fight for victory week-in, week-out now." Antonelli, however, said he had his worst weekend of the season. He started 16th after crashing out of qualifying and finished fifth in the race. That allowed Russell to narrow the gap to Antonelli at the head of the standings from 81 points to 66. Russell said his focus was on winning every race and he wasn't thinking of the title. "If the season were to have started today, or since the summer break, I feel very much I would have been able to fight," he added. "Now I’ve got this big deficit. So I’m not chasing that. I’m chasing to win every race, and what will be, will be."

item.title: México empata ante Colombia en debut de DT Rafael Márquez
item.description: La selección mexicana de fútbol empató el sábado por 1-1 ante su similar de Colombia en la presentación de Rafael Márquez como director técnico del representativo de la Concacaf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La selección mexicana de fútbol empató el sábado por 1-1 ante su similar de Colombia en la presentación de Rafael Márquez como director técnico del representativo de la Concacaf. Márquez fue presentado el 10 de septiembre como director técnico de la selección de México tras haber sido asistente técnico de Javier "Vasco" Aguirre en el pasado Mundial. "En general me gustó mucho el equipo, lo que más me gustó fue la actitud y que mantuvimos una intensidad importante durante casi todo el partido. En términos generales la actitud y dinámica que se impuso, el equipo estuvo bastante bien", dijo Márquez en conferencia de prensa tras el partido. "Mantuvimos la etiqueta con la que hicimos el Mundial que era competir y que no nos minimizamos ante un rival importante, y sí es la etiqueta que queremos llevar. En general, el funcionamiento fue bastante bueno, aunque hay muchas cosas por mejorar todavía, me voy satisfecho pero no conforme", agregó. En el partido disputado en el estadio M&T Bank de Baltimore, Colombia se adelantó a los nueve minutos con un remate de cabeza de Luis Suárez en el área chica tras centro enviado por Richard Rios desde la banda derecha. México estuvo cerca de empatar a los 31 minutos con un disparo de Roberto Alvarado que pegó en el poste derecho. El poste volvió a evitar el gol de México a los 35 minutos cuando un remate de Armando "Hormiga" González se estrelló en el palo derecho. El encuentro transcurrió parejo y con ambas selecciones buscando el gol que México encontró a los 62 minutos cuando Gilberto Mora definió con un potente disparo dentro del área tras eludir al zaguero Jhon Lucumí después de recibir un pase de Jesús Gallardo. Con el empate, los dirigidos por Márquez se motivaron y empezaron a dominar el partido y a generar acciones de peligro que no concretaron. Poco a poco, Colombia emparejó las acciones generando un encuentro muy parejo que ya no tuvo más goles. "Ya sabemos todos la calidad de Gilberto, ahora hay que intentar cuidarlo, protegerlo y que se siga desarrollando, vamos a hacer todo lo posible para que siga creciendo y nos pueda dar más actuaciones como ésta No tengo ninguna duda en que se seguirá desarrollando y dándonos muchísimas alegrías, y ojalá que pronto lo podamos ver en un equipo importante en Europa", señaló Márquez respecto a Mora. El siguiente compromiso de México será el 29 de septiembre ante Perú en el Sports Illustrated Stadium de Nueva Jersey, mismo escenario en el que Colombia enfrentará el 2 de octubre a Paraguay.

item.title: Mariners rookie LHP Kade Anderson exits after hit by line drive vs. Angels
item.description: Seattle Mariners rookie left-hander Kade Anderson left Saturday's game in the fourth inning after taking a line drive from the Los Angeles Angels' Christian Moore off his pitching arm.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Seattle Mariners rookie left-hander Kade Anderson left Saturday's game in the fourth inning after taking a line drive from the Los Angeles Angels' Christian Moore off his pitching arm. Moore hit a liner that appeared to catch Anderson just above his left elbow. Anderson, 22, hopped off the mound in pain as the ball trickled toward first base, with Moore reaching on an infield single. Anderson tried to wave away the Mariners' training staff, but they quickly attended to him and manager Dan Wilson didn't hesitate in calling in Michael Rucker to protect the franchise's prized pitching prospect. Anderson pitched 3 1/3 scoreless innings, giving up four hits. He walked one and struck out four. He entered the day with a 2-2 record, 3.79 ERA, eight walks and 28 strikeouts in 32 1/3 innings over six starts. The host Mariners were leading 2-0 in the fifth inning. Seattle selected Anderson third overall in the 2025 MLB Draft out of LSU. --Field Level Media

item.title: US 'very much' understands Taiwan's defence needs, Taipei official says
item.description: The United States "very much" understands Taiwan's defence needs and the severe military threat it faces from China, a senior Taiwanese diplomat said on Sunday, following a Washington summit between the US and Chinese leaders.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The United States "very much" understands Taiwan's defence needs and the severe military threat it faces from China, a senior Taiwanese diplomat said on Sunday, following a Washington summit between the US and Chinese leaders. Democratically governed Taiwan, which China claims as its own territory, has been waiting for months for US President Donald Trump to approve a new arms sales package worth some $14 billion, following up on a record [USN:L1N3XN16Z TEXT:"$11 billion deal"] unveiled last December. After meeting Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing in May, Trump said he was keeping the latest arms sales package in [USN:L1N41T01D TEXT:"abeyance"]. Trump has not mentioned the sale since last week's summit, saying only on Saturday that Xi understands his [USN:S0N4310B3 TEXT:"position"] on Taiwan. Speaking to reporters in Taipei, Taiwan Deputy Foreign Minister Chen Ming-chi pointed to comments by US Secretary of State [USN:L1N45G08H TEXT:"Marco Rubio"] that military sales to anyone require the same careful consideration. "Taiwan faces a severe situation in the Taiwan Strait. Even though China's economy is declining, it continues investing more resources into building military capacity. Under this context, the US very much understands our defence needs," he said. Washington also understands Taiwan's determination to invest in its military, Chen added. "We do continuously communicate with them, and we believe the US understands the situation we face and our determination on defence investment completely." The United States is bound by law to provide Taiwan with the means to defend itself. China has repeatedly called for military sales to end. David Perdue, the US ambassador to China, told CNBC on Friday that there has been [USN:L1N45I017 TEXT:"no change"] in Taiwan policy by Trump, including on arms sales. Chen said Taiwan had received confirmation "from our American friends repeatedly that US policy toward Taiwan remains unchanged". Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future. China has rebuffed repeated calls for talks by Taiwan President Lai Ching-te, whom it calls a "separatist".

item.title: Hunter Goodman hits 2 HRs as Rockies expel White Sox from AL Central race
item.description: Hunter Goodman went deep twice to surpass 40 home runs and the visiting Colorado Rockies eliminated the Chicago White Sox from the American League Central race with a 9-6 win on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Hunter Goodman went deep twice to surpass 40 home runs and the visiting Colorado Rockies eliminated the Chicago White Sox from the American League Central race with a 9-6 win on Saturday night. Chicago's loss and Cleveland's 11-5 win at Kansas City locked the White Sox (83-78) into the third wild card. They will start the playoffs at the AL West champion, either Houston or Texas. Goodman is the first National League catcher to hit at least 40 home runs since 2003. He reached the mark with a solo shot in the third and added a three-run long ball in the ninth. Nolan Arenado was the last Colorado player to hit 40 home runs when he slugged 41 in 2019. Ezequiel Tovar homered among his two hits and Cole Carrigg added three hits for the Rockies (58-103), who snapped a five-game skid. Andrew Benintendi hit a three-run homer in the ninth, Brenton Doyle and Luisangle Acuna also went deep and Kyle Teel finished with two hits for Chicago. Colorado chased starter Davis Martin after he only got two outs. TJ Rumfield had an RBI single and Adael Amador drove in two with a single to give the Rockies a 3-0 lead. Martin (9-8) allowed three runs (two earned) on three hits before exiting after 25 pitches. Doyle's solo homer in the second, his fifth, cut the deficit to 3-1 and Acuna's second homer of the season in the bottom of the third made it 4-2. Rockies starter Jose Quintana gave up two runs in three innings and Ryan Feltner (7-10) tossed 3 2/3 innings in relief. Tovar matched Acuna's solo shot in the fourth, his 13th of the season, extending Colorado's edge to 5-2. The White Sox cut into the lead in the seventh. Miguel Vargas walked with one out, Andrew Benintendi reached on a fielder's choice and was safe on an error to put runners on the corners. Randal Grichuk drove in a run with a groundout. Chicago had runners on the corners with no outs in the eighth but failed to score. Carrigg had an RBI single in the ninth ahead of Goodman's blast. --Field Level Media

item.title: Report: Bulls trade Rob Dillingham to Hornets for Buddy Hield, cash
item.description: The Chicago Bulls are swapping former first-round pick Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for veteran Buddy Hield and cash, ESPN reported on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Bulls are swapping former first-round pick Rob Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for veteran Buddy Hield and cash, ESPN reported on Saturday. Dillingham, 21, will be on his third NBA team, while Hield, 33, was dealt earlier in the week from the Atlanta Hawks to the Hornets, along with guard Ryan Nembhard and cash, for forward Dorian Finney-Smith. The San Antonio Spurs selected Dillingham with the eighth overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft out of Kentucky and traded him the same day to Minnesota. The Timberwolves dealt Dillingham to the Bulls on Feb. 5, 2026. The point guard averaged 9.6 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 21.5 minutes in 30 games for the Bulls last season as a reserve. For his career, Dillingham has averaged 5.5 points, 1.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 13.0 minutes in 114 games (one start) for the Timberwolves (2024-26) and Bulls. Charlotte announced on Friday that second-year sharpshooter Kon Knueppel suffered a left hamstring injury during an offseason on-court activity and could miss the start of the regular season. Hield has career averages of 14.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 2.4 assists. The guard/forward split last season between the Golden State Warriors (44 games) and Hawks (seven) and averaged a career-low 7.6 points per game. Hield's highest scoring average came in 2018-19 when he put up 20.7 per game for the Sacramento Kings. The Bulls will be Hield's eighth team. He has made 2,201 3-pointers, 15th-most in NBA history, while shooting 39.5% from beyond the arc. The New Orleans Pelicans picked him sixth overall in the 2016 draft out of Oklahoma. --Field Level Media

item.title: Guardians storm past Royals, clinch third straight AL Central title
item.description: Patrick Bailey and Brayan Rocchio homered twice and Chase DeLauter also went deep as the Cleveland Guardians beat the host Kansas City Royals 11-5, and with the Chicago White Sox's loss to the Colorado Rockies, clinched their third consecutive AL Central title Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Patrick Bailey and Brayan Rocchio homered twice and Chase DeLauter also went deep as the Cleveland Guardians beat the host Kansas City Royals 11-5, and with the Chicago White Sox's loss to the Colorado Rockies, clinched their third consecutive AL Central title Saturday night. Rocchio, who posted back-to-back homers with Bailey in the ninth, and Steven Kwan and Travis Bazzana had three hits apiece, while Nathaniel Lowe added four RBIs for the Guardians (85-76), who have won nine of 10 and will receive a bye into the AL Division Series as the No. 2 seed. Cleveland starter Tanner Bibee (7-15) yielded three first-inning runs, then did not allow another run over his six-inning outing. He gave up seven hits, struck out six and walked one. Jac Caglianone had a pair of RBI doubles for Kansas City (68-93), which is in a 6-18 rut. The Royals starter Michael Wacha (9-10) allowed six runs (two earned) and six hits over 6 1/3 innings, striking out four and walking one. The Royals wasted no time getting to Bibee. Carter Jensen opened the first with his first of two doubles, went to third on Bobby Witt Jr.'s bloop single and scored on catcher Bailey's throwing error to second base on Witt's successful steal attempt. Caglianone followed with a run-scoring double and eventually came home via Michael Massey's single for a 3-0 lead. Cleveland rallied to take the lead in a four-run second. Jo Adell reached on Witt's fielding error, went to third on Bazzana's double and scored via a sacrifice fly by Nathaniel Lowe. With two outs, Bailey clanked the right field foul pole for a two-run homer to tie the contest. The Guardians then went ahead when Rocchio doubled and scored on Kwan's triple past diving left fielder Isaac Collins to make it 4-3. Cleveland added on in the third when DeLauter led off with a drive just over the right-center-field fence. In the sixth, Bazzana tripled and scored on another Lowe sacrifice fly. In the seventh with Anthony Gose on the mound, Rocchio sent a high drive that carried beyond the left field wall for a 7-3 Cleveland edge. Kansas City got two runs in the eighth, beginning with back-to-back doubles from Witt and Caglianone off Craig Yoho. Pasquantino added an RBI single. Lowe hit a two-run single to cap the Guardians' four-run ninth. --Field Level Media

item.title: Brice Turang's 2-run homer lifts Brewers past Cardinals
item.description: Brice Turang's two-run homer provided the go-ahead runs and the Milwaukee Brewers bullpen combined for six hitless innings to preserve a 3-2 victory over the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Brice Turang's two-run homer provided the go-ahead runs and the Milwaukee Brewers bullpen combined for six hitless innings to preserve a 3-2 victory over the visiting St. Louis Cardinals on Saturday. Milwaukee (102-59), which has won four straight National League Central Division titles, has clinched a first-round bye and home-field advantage throughout the playoffs. The Brewers, who have had a winning record each month of the season, improved to 17-6 in September. Turang put Milwaukee in front 3-2 in the fifth with a two-run homer off Cardinals starter Quinn Mathews (2-4). Jackson Chourio dribbled a two-out single in front of home plate, and Turang followed with his 21st homer, sending the first pitch 421 feet to center. Brewers starter Dustin May, acquired from St. Louis at the trade deadline, gave up all three Cardinals hits and allowed two runs in three innings before exiting after 58 pitches. Left-hander Kyle Harrison (11-5), whose second-half struggles cost him a spot in the rotation, followed with two scoreless innings for his first victory since Aug. 18. JoJo Romero and Antonio Senzatela combined for two scoreless innings, and Aaron Ashby covered the final two innings for his fourth save. Mathews allowed three runs on five hits in five innings, striking out seven and walking two. The Cardinals (77-84) took a 1-0 lead in the second inning when Jordan Walker hit a leadoff single and stole second base. Thomas Saggese's two-out single to left scored Walker. Alec Burleson put St. Louis up 2-0 in the third with his 26th homer and third in three games, a two-out solo shot to right-center off May. The Brewers got one back in the bottom half when Brandon Lockridge doubled to open, advanced on a sacrifice bunt and came home on Chourio's RBI single to right. --Field Level Media

item.title: Bangkok floodwaters recede after torrential rain as residents count losses
item.description: Floodwaters receded in many parts of the Thai capital Bangkok on Sunday after torrential rain eased, even as residents in some flooded neighbourhoods remained stranded in their homes.
item.dc:creator: Napat Wesshasartar, Chayut Setboonsarng
item.content:encoded: Floodwaters receded in many parts of the Thai capital Bangkok on Sunday after torrential rain eased, even as residents in some flooded neighbourhoods remained stranded in their homes. The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration declared the capital a [USN:L6N45I01O TEXT:"disaster-affected"] area on Saturday after nearly 300 mm (12 inches) of rain fell over 48 hours, leading to flooding on major roads that left some cars partly submerged. Arita Sanpoka, 33, a resident of a flooded community, said two neighbours in their 80s remained stranded in their home because they could not get downstairs. "Right now the water in my house is up to waist height," Arita said. "Everything in the house is ruined." She said daily life had become difficult, with power cut off on the ground floor and the bathroom unusable as the water level continued to rise. The BMA said 233 temporary shelters had been prepared and about 4,200 people were using the facilities. The flooding affected neighbourhoods across the capital, with water entering homes and disrupting transport. Some areas became difficult to access, while residents were forced to wade through the water. Rachthanichporn Leeput, 37, said she walked 2 to 3 km (1 to 2 miles) through water after flooding in her area occurred rapidly on Friday evening. "The water rose very fast," she said. "Many people, many households, couldn't prepare in time." Rachthanichporn, a delivery rider, said the flooding had also cut off her income. She had been wading through the water to buy supplies and resell them to make up for lost earnings. The BMA said on Sunday that rainfall had eased after a low-pressure system that had affected Bangkok over the previous days moved westward. Rain was expected to be lighter, although water levels in several major canals remained high as water continued to flow in from surrounding areas, it said. The weather agency forecasts widespread thunderstorms and isolated heavy rain for Monday. Authorities were continuing to pump water from major canals and assist residents in areas where flooding remained severe.

item.title: China conducts naval, air exercise around disputed shoal in South China Sea
item.description: China's military conducted a joint naval and air training exercise around a disputed shoal in the South China Sea, it said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's military conducted a joint naval and air training exercise around a disputed shoal in the South China Sea, it said on Sunday. The training was held in the waters and airspace around the [USN:L4N43X19V TEXT:"Scarborough Shoal"], which China calls Huangyan Dao. It is also claimed by the Philippines, where it is known as Bajo de Masinloc. The People's Liberation Army Southern Theater Command, in a statement on WeChat, described the operation as a necessary response to actions by "certain countries" it said had undermined regional peace and stability. The People's Liberation Army Southern Theater Command said the training "aims to test and enhance combat capabilities in safeguarding China’s territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests". A separate statement on WeChat from China Coast Guard spokesperson Jiang Lue said the coast guard had conducted drills focused on operations including boarding and inspection, intrusion interdiction and forced towing on Sunday. The Philippine embassy in Beijing did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the Chinese military training.

item.title: Oregon star QB Dante Moore leaves game vs. USC in ambulance
item.description: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was carted off the field following a late hit by Southern California linebacker Desman Stephens II in first half of the No. 20 Ducks' 41-27 victory over the No. 12 Trojans on Saturday night in Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was carted off the field following a late hit by Southern California linebacker Desman Stephens II in first half of the No. 20 Ducks' 41-27 victory over the No. 12 Trojans on Saturday night in Los Angeles. Moore was placed on a stretcher and taken directly into an ambulance. He was able to move his fingers and feet and rotate his arms, and was taken to Los Angeles General Medical Center, per the NBC broadcast. An Oregon spokesperson later said that Moore had movement in all of his extremities and was being evaluated. "He's in recovery, so I'm not going to speak too soon. But he is moving," Ducks head coach Dan Lanning said after the game. "He has the ability to move. So we continue to assess him." During the play with 10:06 remaining in the second quarter, the senior quarterback took off on a scramble. When attempting to slide, he was hit in the head by Stephens, who was called for targeting and disqualified from the game. "It was a disgusting play," Lanning said. "The energy changed. A lot of guys on the sideline, they were emotional in that moment, including myself." Fights broke out between players at midfield while Moore lay on the ground, and both teams were penalized for unsportsmanlike conduct. Backup quarterback Dylan Raiola, who transferred from Nebraska, took over in his place. Moore was 8-of-10 passing for 77 yards, and Raiola was 19 of 25 for 289 yards and two touchdown passes. Moore was an All-Big Ten third-team selection last season, throwing for 3,565 yards, 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions as the team went 13-2. This season, he was off to a strong start with 849 passing yards and nine passing touchdowns in three games. Moore spent his freshman season at UCLA in 2023 and played in nine games before transferring to Oregon for the 2024 season. --Field Level Media

item.title: Protesters block Orange Order from marching through Catholic area in Northern Ireland
item.description: Around 2,000 protesters blocked the way into a Catholic area in a Northern Irish town that a Protestant parade was due to walk down on Sunday morning after the lifting of an almost 30-year ban on a route that was a flashpoint of sectarian disputes.
item.dc:creator: Cathal McNaughton
item.content:encoded: Around 2,000 protesters blocked the way into a Catholic area in a Northern Irish town that a Protestant parade was due to walk down on Sunday morning after the lifting of an almost 30-year ban on a route that was a flashpoint of sectarian disputes. Crowds including Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill of Irish nationalists Sinn Fein and the party's leader, Mary Lou McDonald, gathered in the rain on the Garvaghy Road overnight after Belfast's High Court [USN:S8N44V002 TEXT:"dismissed an application"] by residents to stop the parade early on Sunday morning. Annual attempts by the Protestant Orange Order to march through the area triggered unrest across the British-run region before the route was banned in 1998, the same year the Good Friday Agreement largely ended the three decades of violence known as the "Troubles". "This is madness," McDonald told reporters on the road, a Catholic enclave in the largely Protestant town of Portadown. "This, in fact, is primitive treatment of any community in the year 2026. It is intolerable." British Prime Minister Andy Burnham called for calm on Sunday. "I know it's a tense situation, we do appeal for calm on all sides. There have been big gains made in Northern Ireland and we don't want to see things go backwards," Burnham told the BBC. He said he had spoken to Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin on the matter on Saturday. Northern Ireland's Parades Commission - which regulates marches in the British-run region - [USN:L8N45H0SR TEXT:"on Friday permitted"] that a smaller-than-usual 35 people could take part in the march between 8 a.m. (0700 GMT) and 9:30 a.m. ORANGE SASHES AND BOWLER HATS A small group of Orange Order members wearing traditional silk orange sashes and black bowler hats gathered at another part of the town but the march had not started by 9:30 a.m. A senior member told the BBC that the group would wait for police to tell them the route was ready for them to start. Police vans parked near the Garvaghy Road had earlier played out a warning that anyone taking part in the protest was committing a criminal offence. The Drumcree dispute exploded in the mid-1990s when, in the wake of ceasefires by Northern Ireland's main guerrilla groups, it became a symbol of the wider dispute between mainly Catholic nationalists, who consider themselves Irish, and Protestants loyal to Britain. The Orangemen, who take their name from Protestant King William of Orange who defeated deposed Catholic King James II at the Battle of the Boyne in 1690, say their parades are part of their Protestant cultural tradition. Whilst most of the parades that take place across Northern Ireland each year are uncontroversial, nationalists say parades such as Drumcree passing through Catholic areas are an offensive display of triumphalism designed to intimidate them. PEACE PROCESS BROUGHT 'INTO QUESTION' McDonald and O'Neill called on the British government and police to intervene. O'Neill said she had spoken to Britain's minister for the region and the Irish government. The Irish government issued a statement saying it was very concerned about the situation and that its primary concern was to "avoid a return to the divisions of the past." "I think that this brings into question how this whole peace process works," said O'Neill, whose party rules alongside the largest pro-British party in a devolved power-sharing administration that was a key part of the 1998 peace deal. The governing Democratic Unionist Party, some of whose lawmakers stood alongside the Orange Order, said the march must be allowed to proceed. "A First Minister's duty is to uphold lawful decisions, not inflame opposition to them," DUP leader Gavin Robinson said in a statement. Northern Ireland's police chief, Jon Boutcher, appealed in a statement to "everyone to remain calm and peaceful", and urged those with influence to encourage people to comply with the law and work with the police.

item.title: Cruz Azul saca empate de último minuto con gol de uruguayo "Toro" Fernández en torneo mexicano
item.description: Cruz Azul, actual campeón del fútbol mexicano, sacó el sábado un empate por 3-3 ante Toluca gracias a un gol del uruguayo Gabriel "Toro" Fernández en tiempo de reposición del partido correspondiente a la décima jornada del torneo Apertura.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Cruz Azul, actual campeón del fútbol mexicano, sacó el sábado un empate por 3-3 ante Toluca gracias a un gol del uruguayo Gabriel "Toro" Fernández en tiempo de reposición del partido correspondiente a la décima jornada del torneo Apertura. Con la igualada, la "Máquina Celeste" de Cruz Azul llegó a 16 puntos para mantenerse en el sexto lugar de la tabla de posiciones que continúan liderando los "Diablos Rojos" de Toluca con 20 unidades. "El objetivo es seguir generando para obtener un legado, tenemos que mejorar la parte defensiva y el control emocional. Si hacemos bien las correcciones no tengo dudas de que vamos a mejorar, veremos un equipo completo, con un buen cierre de torneo y peleando por un título más ", dijo el director técnico de Cruz Azul, Joel Huiqui. En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de Ciudad de México, el argentino Nicolás Ibáñez puso en ventaja a Cruz Azul a los siete minutos cuando definió con un disparo cruzado dentro del área tras recibir un pase de su compatriota José Antonio Paradela, quien robó el balón en la media cancha. El "Toro" Fernández anotó el segundo gol a los 38 minutos cuando se elevó entre dos jugadores de Toluca para rematar con la cabeza un centro enviado por Ibáñez desde el sector derecho. La reacción de Toluca inició en la segunda parte del partido y descontó a los 55 minutos por la vía del tiro penal que anotó el brasileño Helio Nunes "Helinho". La árbitra Katia Itzel García señaló la pena máxima después de revisar en el VAR una jugada donde el defensor colombiano Willer Ditta sujetó dentro del área al brasileño Luan García. Un minuto después, Toluca empató cuando Alexis Vega sorprendió al portero Andrés Gudiño con un disparo desde fuera del área. El equipo visitante dio la vuelta al marcador a los 78 minutos con un potente disparo de Vega desde fuera del área tras recibir un pase del argentino Nicolás Castro, quien aprovechó un mal control de Carlos Rodríguez para robarle el balón. Cuando parecía que Toluca se llevaría el triunfo, el "Toro" Fernández marcó su doblete y dio el empate a Cruz Azul con un remate de cabeza en el área chica tras centro enviado desde el sector izquierdo por Andrés Montaño a los 95 minutos. "Siempre que vamos ganando nos cuesta, es un punto a trabajar, equilibrar entre la fase defensiva y ofensiva. Tratamos de trabajar en la regularidad, en el equilibrio, en cómo poder manejar las emociones, somos un equipo maduro, pero por momentos caemos en emociones descontroladas”, reconoció Huiqui. En otros partidos, Querétaro venció por 2-0 como visitante a Guadalajara con goles de Ali Ávila y del argentino Mateo Coronel. Santos Laguna ganó por 1-0 a Pachuca con gol del español Francisco Villalba, mientras que Tigres UANL derrotó por 1-0 a Puebla con tanto del argentino Juan Francisco Brunetta. La jornada se completará el domingo cuando Pumas UNAM enfrente al Atlético de San Luis, León juegue ante Bravos de Ciudad Juárez y América visite a Necaxa. El viernes, Atlante venció por 4-2 a Monterrey, y Atlas ganó por 3-2 como visitante a Tijuana.

item.title: 2-time All-Star Kirby Yates announces retirement
item.description: Right-hander Kirby Yates announced his retirement following the Pittsburgh Pirates' 4-3 loss to the Detroit Tigers on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Right-hander Kirby Yates announced his retirement following the Pittsburgh Pirates' 4-3 loss to the Detroit Tigers on Saturday. "I don't have anything left. Let's put it that way," Yates said after the game. "I've been running on fumes for a while, and I think it's just time and it's felt like it's been time for a little while now." Yates made the first start of his major league career Saturday, working 1 2/3 scoreless innings while allowing two hits and striking out one. Yates played 12 seasons in the major leagues with the Tampa Bay Rays (2014-15), New York Yankees (2016), Los Angeles Angels (2017, 2026), San Diego Padres (2017-20), Atlanta Braves (2022-23), Texas Rangers (2024), Los Angeles Dodgers (2025) and Pittsburgh Pirates (2026). For his career, the veteran appeared in 518 games, recording 101 saves and 672 strikeouts with a 3.35 ERA and 1.14 WHIP. His best season came in 2019 with the Padres, when he led the majors with 41 saves and posted a 1.19 ERA. Yates earned his second All-Star selection in 2024 with the Rangers, posting 33 saves and a career-best 1.17 ERA. The 39-year-old began the 2026 campaign with the Angels. He was traded to the Pirates in August. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers start strong in win over Twins to keep pace in AL West
item.description: Danny Jansen went 2-for-4 with a homer and two RBIs, and the Texas Rangers jumped ahead early in their 6-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Saturday evening in Minneapolis.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Danny Jansen went 2-for-4 with a homer and two RBIs, and the Texas Rangers jumped ahead early in their 6-2 win over the Minnesota Twins on Saturday evening in Minneapolis. Jake Burger also homered for Texas (80-81), which continues to hold serve in its bid to knock off the Houston Astros (80-81) for first place in the American League West division. However, with Houston's 13-2 win over the Athletics late Saturday evening, the Rangers need to win and see the Astros lose on Sunday in order to win the division and make the postseason as Houston holds the tiebreaker advantage. Evan Carter and Alejandro Osuna each finished with two hits and an RBI for Texas. Kody Clemens and Josh Bell had one RBI apiece for Minnesota (76-85). Rangers left-hander Robert Garcia (2-1) earned the victory with 1 2/3 scoreless innings of relief. He followed starter Nathan Eovaldi, who allowed one run on four hits in 4 1/3 innings. Twins right-hander Bailey Ober (7-7) surrendered six runs on 10 hits in five innings. He walked one and struck out five. The Twins opened the scoring with a run in the bottom of the first inning. Luke Keaschall hit a leadoff double, advanced to third on a groundout by Brooks Lee and scored on an RBI groundout by Clemens. The Rangers answered with a four-run outburst in the second, scoring all of the runs after the first two batters of the inning were retired. Nicky Lopez started the rally with a double. He scored one batter later as Jansen singled and Alan Roden committed a throwing error in left field. Carter put the Rangers on top 2-1 with an RBI double to right in the next at-bat. Osuna followed with an RBI double, and Nimmo capped the big inning with another RBI double to make it 4-1. Texas made it 5-1 when Jansen led off the fourth with a 398-foot homer to left. The power surge continued in the fifth. Burger hit a 415-foot solo shot to center to increase the Rangers' lead to 6-1. The Twins pulled within 6-2 in the eighth when Bell's RBI single followed Keaschall's leadoff triple. Before the game, the Rangers placed third baseman Josh Jung on the injured list and recalled catcher Logan O'Hoppe from Triple-A Round Rock. Jung was hit on the wrist by a pitch in the first inning of Friday's 10-2 loss. The start of the game was delayed two hours because of rain. -Field Level Media

item.title: Yuna Nishimura cards another 63; leads by 5 in Arkansas
item.description: Japan's Yuna Nishimura carded her second consecutive 8-under-par 63 on Saturday and stretched her lead to five strokes over the field at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship in Rogers, Ark.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japan's Yuna Nishimura carded her second consecutive 8-under-par 63 on Saturday and stretched her lead to five strokes over the field at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship in Rogers, Ark. Nishimura, 26, who is in search of her first LPGA Tournament victory, did make her first bogey of the weekend but more than made up for it with nine birdies to complete 36 holes at 16 under. Auston Kim and Chinese golfers Mary Liu and Michelle Zhang all followed up 4-under-par rounds of 67 on Friday with scores of 7-under 64 on Saturday and got to the clubhouse at 11 under. Nine players were six shots off of Nishimura's pace, including England's Lottie Woad and Charley Hull and 30-year old American Sophia Schubert. Nishimura hit two fewer fairways but shaved three putts off her Friday round. For the second consecutive day, she birdied her first hole of the day -- the par-4 10th. She birdied five of seven holes in the middle of the round, then closed birdie-birdie-par to position herself ideally for her first title. "My short irons were working really well so I was able to put it close to the pin and kind of all worked out for me," said Nishimura. The 26-year-old Kim is right back out on the course after making her Solheim Cup debut last week. Like Nishimura, she is searching for her first career title, but she has four top-10 finishes in 2026. After a topsy-turvy round which featured two eagles and two double bogeys on Friday, Kim produced a bogey-free round on Saturday, finishing with back-to-back birdies on her final two holes (Nos. 8 and 9). "I hit two really bad shots (Friday) that cost me, and it's not to say that I didn't hit any bad shots today, but just being able to minimize the really, really bad ones," said Kim. "Thankfully I didn't hit a lot of those today. Just staying positive and trying to be really aggressive to my targets and make as many putts as I can." The former Vanderbilt golfer admits to not being "100%" this week, but she truly enjoyed her experience in the Netherlands. "I had the time of my life with all the girls last week, and it was probably the most I've enjoyed playing golf and competing and just being a competitor out there," she said. Lauren Coughlin set an LPGA Tour record with nine consecutive birdies to begin her round, putting her in position to shatter Annika Sorenstam's Tour record of 59 for lowest score in a round. But Coughlin birdied just once on the back nine and finished with a 10-under 61. She is tied for 21st at 8 under thanks to a first-round 73. Miya Yamashita, also from Japan, tied Nishimura with a 63 on Saturday, but the two-time winner in 2026 carded a 70 on Friday and is seven shots behind her countrywoman. Nishimura plans to stay calm, yet focused on her final round on Sunday. "So it's going to be the same thing again (Sunday), but I would like to go for 20 under..." she said. "Things are going well so I really don't want to change anything." Given her play so far at the Pinnacle Country Club layout, 20 under seems like a modest goal. --Field Level Media

item.title: Wild D Brock Faber day-to-day after taking puck to head
item.description: Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber is considered day-to-day after being struck on the side of the head by a shot during Friday's preseason finale against the Dallas Stars.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Minnesota Wild defenseman Brock Faber is considered day-to-day after being struck on the side of the head by a shot during Friday's preseason finale against the Dallas Stars. Faber did not practice Saturday, though coach John Hynes said the 24-year-old is "doing well" as the Wild continue to monitor his condition. Minnesota has not ruled Faber out for Thursday's regular-season opener at Nashville. "You've got to let some things resolve," Hynes said. "Some of it was precautionary. It's a delicate area." Faber was struck near his left ear by a shot from Dallas forward Sam Steel during the second period Friday. He immediately went down but eventually skated to the bench without assistance. Faber finished the period before sitting out the third. Hynes said the Wild expect to have a clearer picture after a 24-to-48-hour evaluation period. Minnesota recalled defenseman Carson Lambos from Iowa of the American Hockey League on Saturday to add depth while Faber is unavailable. Without Faber, the Wild practiced with Quinn Hughes alongside Jared Spurgeon, Jonas Brodin paired with Olli Maatta and Daemon Hunt skating with Zach Bogosian. Minnesota must submit its season-opening roster Monday. --Field Level Media
